name: Cham cheo
summary: The Thái dipping sauce. Vietnam News grinds mắc khén with salt, fresh and dried chilli, garlic, and broth mix. Vietnamnet dry-roasts the mắc khén and adds lemongrass and dried coriander. The recipes disagree. The culture desk does not use the name in the fish recipe. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Dien Bien Phu. Vietnam News also spells it chẳm chéo. Vietnamnet spells it chẳm chéo and chéo. Both spellings stay.
taste: Vietnamnet says the smell is sharp and herbal rather than soft, and that the sharpness is the mountain character of the sauce.
howToEat: Vietnam News, quoting Lê Thị Duyên: mắc khén mixed with salt, grilled fresh chilli, dried chilli, garlic, and broth mix, ground together into a viscous sauce.
Vietnamnet: dry-roast the mắc khén fruit, pound it fine, and mix it with seedless dried chilli toasted crisp, roasted salt, dried coriander leaf pounded fine, and lemongrass.
Vietnamnet names it as the dip for xôi nếp nương, cabbage-wrapped oleaster, forest meat, and grilled fish. The culture desk’s fish recipe does not use the name. A price is Check on arrival.
where: The Thái table. Vietnam News quotes Lê Thị Duyên on the sauce and does not print a street. A stall hour is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Cham cheo in Dien Bien Phu — two recipes
seoDescription: Thái dipping sauce. Vietnam News uses chilli, garlic, and broth mix. Vietnamnet uses roasted mắc khén, lemongrass, and dried coriander. A price is Check on arrival.
